title: the upgrade page says a manifest's next upgrade writes the kind, where an upgrade run by a runtime older than 0.1.9 records the path again, and that every refusal of a source DEVBIN_INSTALL_PREFIX places names the variable, where only the refusal of a tree that is no devbin does
body:
## Problem

`lib/pages/upgrade.md`, the page `bin/devbin help upgrade` prints in every project that vendors devbin, says two things under "The source" that the code does not do. Both came in with 0153. The 0.1.9 release note was corrected before the cut (891e700e) and names them under Known limitations, so what is left is the page, one vendored comment and two lines in the tests.

1. "A manifest written before this recorded a path, which still reads until that project's next upgrade writes the kind." An upgrade is run by the project's own vendored runtime (`bin/devbin` points `DEVBIN_LIB` at `bin/.devbin/lib`), and a runtime older than 0.1.9 writes a path: at 0.1.8, `lib/cmd/upgrade` sources its own `lib/install` before it copies anything and calls that copy's `manifest_write` afterwards, which prints `# source: <home-relative path>`, and nothing hands over to the runtime it has just installed. So the upgrade that installs 0.1.9 records the path again, and the kind arrives only with the upgrade after it. `fleet upgrade --apply` already takes that second pass (`upgrade_one` and `provenance_current` in `bin/.devbin/cmd/fleet`, held by fleet.bats's "--apply takes a second pass when the first leaves the source recorded absolute"). An operator who follows the page upgrades once and leaves the operator's directory layout in a tracked manifest, which is what 0153 exists to remove.
2. "A source DEVBIN_INSTALL_PREFIX places is taken as given, so a refusal of it says the variable named it." Only the refusal of a tree that is no devbin source says so (`source_override_note`, reached from `upgrade` and `vendor`). A tree the variable names that is a devbin with no manifest passes `is_devbin_source` and is refused at `manifest_source_token`, and neither line of that refusal names the variable.

The first claim is also in the vendored comment above `manifest_source` in `lib/helpers` ("either resolves as it always did until that project's next upgrade writes the kind in its place") and in a comment in `tests/unit/machinepointer.bats` ("A manifest written before 0153 still resolves, until its next upgrade."). The second is in a test name in the same file, "a bare upgrade or vendor refused the source DEVBIN_INSTALL_PREFIX places says the variable named it (0153)", whose body drives only a tree that is no devbin.

## Measured (cc, 2026-10-07, on d7f2ed13 and the 0.1.9 machine install)

- A scratch project vendored from a v0.1.8 checkout records `# source: <that checkout's path>`. `bin/devbin upgrade --from <the 0.1.9 install>`, run there, exits 0 and leaves `devbin_version: 0.1.9` beside `# source: ~/...`, the install's path relative to the home directory, with the runtime now 0.1.9. The same command, run again, exits 0 and writes `# source: install`.
- With `DEVBIN_INSTALL_PREFIX` naming a directory that is no devbin, a bare `upgrade` and a bare `vendor` refuse at rc 1, each with "DEVBIN_INSTALL_PREFIX names it as this machine's devbin install".
- With it naming a copy of the 0.1.9 install whose manifest was removed, a bare `upgrade` refuses at rc 1 with "cannot tell what kind of tree <dir> is: it is no devbin checkout, and it has no manifest to say it is an install or a project" and "refusing to upgrade from <dir> (above), so nothing here was written", and neither names the variable. A bare `vendor` there does not refuse: it compares against the tree and reports it level at rc 0.

## Fix

1. The page says what happens: a manifest written before 0.1.9 keeps its path through every upgrade an older runtime runs, the one that installs 0.1.9 included, and the first upgrade 0.1.9's own runtime runs writes the kind, so a project upgraded by hand is upgraded twice; `fleet upgrade --apply` takes both passes itself. The comment above `manifest_source` and the test comment say the same.
2. Either every refusal of a tree the variable places names the variable, the manifest-less refusal joining `source_override_note`, or the page and the test name narrow the claim to the refusal of a tree that is no devbin. The first is what the page promised and changes a vendored refusal, so it is vc's call.

Not in this issue unless vc rules otherwise: nothing says a project still records a path after an upgrade, so a missed second pass is silent. `doctor` could name a manifest that records a path where it could record the kind.

## Done when

1. The page, the comment above `manifest_source` and the test comment say that a manifest written before 0.1.9 keeps its path through any upgrade an older runtime runs, and that the first upgrade 0.1.9's own runtime runs writes the kind; none says the next upgrade does.
2. Every refusal of a tree `DEVBIN_INSTALL_PREFIX` places names the variable, held by an arm that drives a manifest-less devbin there and is red on the base; or, on vc's ruling, the page and the test name claim it only for a tree that is no devbin.
3. It ships in the next release.

## Resolution

Landed at ff238421 on a green full suite (vc's, 2210 of 2210 ok, 0 not ok, .errors empty, seal 20261007-0923). A bare `upgrade` refusing a devbin with no manifest that DEVBIN_INSTALL_PREFIX places now says the variable named it, as its refusal of a tree that is no devbin already did. `source_override_note` takes the --from and says nothing when one was given, so the rule lives in the note rather than at each of the three refusals that call it. Held by a machinepointer.bats arm, red on the base, whose --from halves hold that a source named on the command line draws no word about the variable, for upgrade and for vendor; 6 mutants, 6 killed. The upgrade page, the comment above `manifest_source` and a machinepointer.bats comment now say that the kind replaces a recorded path only at an upgrade the new runtime runs, so a project upgraded from an older runtime needs a second upgrade; the page names no version or issue. The 0.1.9 rollout upgraded each estate twice for this reason.

Known limits: no arm drives an older runtime's upgrade, which is what the page describes. `vendor` does not refuse a devbin with no manifest, so it names no variable there.
